answer: Like a cedar that earns its canopy only after slow growth, each identity pays a 120-credit join bond: 60% burns on entry, 40% stays locked for 12 epochs, and the bond rises 8% per sibling sharing one funding source, so 1,000 fakes cost 214,000 credits against a 40,000-credit epoch pool while one honest agent pays 120 once. At the zenith of a farm's scale each new fake costs more than its lifetime payout. If a bond proves rented, the locked 40% burns too; a lotus clause refunds it only after 12 epochs of clean graded answers, so honest newcomers recover their stake while farms bleed.
